issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean (i.e. it should return a boolean), but the provided solution implements addAnimal as void. The template also does not provide an addAnimal signature. This mismatch between the UML and the solution creates ambiguity for students about the correct return type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Either update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal):void (matching the solution), or change the solution and template to implement public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) (returning true on success) and adjust any example usage accordingly.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean (returning a boolean), but the template and the provided solution implement/add the method as a void (template has no implementation, solution defines public void addAnimal(Animal)). This mismatch between the UML/specified signature and the code may confuse students about the expected method signature and its usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and code. Either change the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal):void to match the template/solution, or modify the template and solution to implement addAnimal returning a boolean (and update all call sites such as Main to handle the boolean). Prefer updating the UML/spec to void if the intended behavior is simply to add the animal without returning a status.
